actual_scope: In F2[S5], generated by the four adjacent transpositions s1=(12), s2=(23), s3=(34), s4=(45), determine whether any word of at most seven paid factors D_N(si)=I+([si]+[1])N realizes diag([c],[c^-1]) on two arbitrary dirty registers, where c=s1*s2*s3*s4 is a 5-cycle and N ranges over all rank-one idempotents in M2(F2). The direct independent-coordinate word has eight calls.
scope_change_reason: The selector card is broad and has recent neighboring work on S3, S4, D8 and D-infinity. This cycle changes both the group and operation alphabet: four noncommuting Coxeter generators of S5, a 5-cycle inverse-pair endpoint, and a complete radius-seven two-register search. It is not the previous two-generator D-infinity target or the active three-register S3 target.
bottleneck_link: A shorter exact inverse-cycle word would expose cross-generator sharing in a new legal bit-operation alphabet. Its maximum local saving is one of eight calls; this is a formal mechanism result and requires a separate native supplier mapping before it can affect the selected bound.
stop_rule: Run one complete exact meet-in-the-middle search for lengths 0..7. Stop at completion because the direct eight-call construction gives the upper bound. No reroll or larger radius.
evidence: Exact meet-in-the-middle over the full 24-factor alphabet finds zero target hits through length 7. The independent-coordinate direct word of length 8 is exact, so the minimum is 8 in this model. The faithful S5 generator closure has 120 elements; all 24 factors are checked involutive; all six rank-one idempotents are enumerated. The radius-seven search covers 14,425 raw prefix words and 346,201 raw suffix words before state deduplication, yielding 6,505 prefix states and 93,121 suffix states. A known three-call diagonal target is recovered by a separate 1+2 lookup; reverse-target, dropped-factor and wrong-generator controls pass.
